answer: No. Your records show you were checked for a blood clot in your lung, but none was found. On 8 July 2025 you had a D-dimer blood test, which was raised at 0.92 (normal is up to 0.49). A raised D-dimer is common and not specific, so it led to a CT scan of the chest with contrast, done that night to look for a clot. The scan report says: 'No pulmonary embolism. Lungs are clear. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine.' The 'pulmonary embolism' entry on your problem list was marked as refuted (ruled out) and resolved the same day. Your chest pain was recorded as chest wall pain, which was noted as resolved by 22 July 2025. The records don't show any later clot diagnosis, and I found no blood thinner prescribed. They don't show what treatment, if any, was given for the chest wall pain.
short: CT angiogram of the chest on 2025-07-08 showed no pulmonary embolism (raised D-dimer 0.92 led to the scan); the PE diagnosis was recorded as refuted and the pain was labeled chest wall pain.
